# `js/jsdoc-no-restricted-syntax`

**No JSDoc block the project restricts**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-js` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-js` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | no preset — name it in `[rules]` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | `contexts`, `entries` |
| **Fix** | `manual` — no automatic fix; the steps are under *How to fix* (what replaces the restricted block is the project's convention) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.2 |
| **Ported from** | `eslint-plugin-jsdoc/no-restricted-syntax` |

## What it checks

A JSDoc block is reported when it documents code of an entry's `context` kind (default `any`), carries its `tag` and its text matches `matches`; `message` replaces `Syntax is restricted: <context> with <tag>`, and may use `{{context}}` and `{{comment}}`. `contexts` is the short form, node kinds only, reporting every block on that code; `entries` names each restriction. A `context` is a tree-sitter node kind of the code a block documents (`function_declaration`, `class_declaration`, `lexical_declaration`, `method_definition` …; the declaration under an `export`, and the function or class a variable holds, count too) or `any`. Upstream names these with esquery selectors over ESTree and the JSDoc AST, which have no equivalent here; a context here is a node kind, and what a block must hold is a `tag` it carries and a `matches` regular expression its text matches. eslint-plugin-jsdoc 65.4.2's `no-restricted-syntax`, read and reimplemented; where upstream reports that its `contexts` option is missing, this rule says nothing.

With no `contexts` or `entries` set the rule is silent: it reports nothing, not even that the option is missing, and the engine does not run it on a single node. It is in no preset; a project switches it on by setting the option under `[rules]` (or in a `[scope.<name>]` for some files).

In `codelaw.toml`, under `[rules]`: `"js/jsdoc-no-restricted-syntax" = { severity = "error", options = { entries = { typeTag = { tag = "type" } } } }`.

**Why:** A TypeScript project keeps types out of its comments, or a project retires a tag; the rule finds the blocks that still carry it.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-js
pip install codelaw-rules-js
```

**No preset turns it on.** Load its pack through any preset (`codelaw:js/recommended` here), then name the rule in `[rules]`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:js/recommended"]

[rules]
"js/jsdoc-no-restricted-syntax" = "error"
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"js/jsdoc-no-restricted-syntax" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `contexts` | `string[]` | `[]` | node kinds of code whose JSDoc block is reported (`function_declaration` …, or `any`) |
| `entries` | `object` | `{}` | named restrictions, each `{ context, tag, matches, message }` |

**Every option at its default** — a starting point to copy:

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-no-restricted-syntax"]
severity = "error"

[rules."js/jsdoc-no-restricted-syntax".options]
contexts = []
entries = {}
```

**The same, inline, with example values:**

```toml
[rules]
"js/jsdoc-no-restricted-syntax" = { severity = "error", options = { contexts = ["function_declaration"], entries = { typeTag = { tag = "type" } } } }
```

- **A table without `severity`** changes only the options: the severity stays what a preset or an earlier layer set, and a rule that is off stays off.
- **A list option replaces its default** — copy the default entries you want to keep.
- **An unknown option or a value of the wrong type** stops the run with exit 2 and names the nearest option.

#### `contexts`

*string[]* · default `[]`

node kinds of code whose JSDoc block is reported (`function_declaration` …, or `any`)

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-no-restricted-syntax".options]
contexts = ["function_declaration"]
```

#### `entries`

*object* · default `{}`

named restrictions, each `{ context, tag, matches, message }`

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-no-restricted-syntax".options]
entries = { typeTag = { tag = "type" } }
```

### Options in action

Each case below is one of the rule's tests (`packs/js/rules/js/jsdoc-no-restricted-syntax.cases.md`): the options, the input, and what codelaw reports.

#### a tag

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-no-restricted-syntax".options]
entries = { typeTag = { tag = "type" } }
```

```js
/** @type {string} */
const name = "x";
/** The age. */
const age = 1;
```

**Reports** at `1:1`.

#### a context

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-no-restricted-syntax".options]
contexts = ["function_declaration"]
```

```js
/** A. */
function a() {}
/** B. */
class B {}
```

**Reports** at `1:1`.

#### a text

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-no-restricted-syntax".options]
entries = { old = { matches = "Deprecated:" } }
```

```js
/** Deprecated: use b. */
function a() {}
```

**Reports** at `1:1`.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/jsdoc-no-restricted-syntax" = { options = { contexts = ["function_declaration"] } } }
```

Or switch it off there:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/jsdoc-no-restricted-syntax" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"js/jsdoc-no-restricted-syntax" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"js/jsdoc-no-restricted-syntax" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"js/jsdoc-no-restricted-syntax" = { severity = "warn", options = { contexts = ["function_declaration"] } }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "js/jsdoc-no-restricted-syntax": {"severity": "warn", "options": {"contexts": ["function_declaration"]}}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore js/jsdoc-no-restricted-syntax: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore js/jsdoc-no-restricted-syntax expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule js/jsdoc-no-restricted-syntax --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain js/jsdoc-no-restricted-syntax       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule js/jsdoc-no-restricted-syntax  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>                 # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Remove or rewrite the block as the project's message says.

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

*With these options:* `{ entries = { typeTag = { tag = "type" } } }`

```js
/** @type {string} */
const name = "x";
```

#### Do

*With these options:* `{ entries = { typeTag = { tag = "type" } } }`

```js
/** The name. */
const name = "x";
```
